claims.statement: com.caozhihu.tmall.util.Page is a four-field bean — start, count, total, param — whose public static final defaultCount is 5 and whose no-arg constructor assigns count = defaultCount; because the pager never emits page.count, every link the UI produces yields a Page whose count came from that constructor.

Page derives all pager metadata arithmetically: getTotalPage() returns ceil(total/count) but never less than 1, and getLast() returns the start offset of the final slice clamped at 0, so an empty table still reports one page and no negative offset.

Page.isHasPreviouse() is true unless start is 0, and isHasNext() compares start against getLast() — the start offset of the last page rather than a page index — which is what adminPage.jsp uses to disable the first/previous and next/last controls.

Page.getTotalPage() and getLast() divide by count while count is request-bindable through Page.setCount and Action4Pagination.setPage, so a request that binds page.count=0 makes the JSP render fail with a division by zero instead of showing an empty page; no caller in the tree does so today.

web/include/admin/adminPage.jsp is the only pagination control in the tree: the paged list shells (listCategory.jsp, listProperty.jsp, listProduct.jsp, listUser.jsp, listOrder.jsp) include it inside a div.pageDiv, and it declares no taglib of its own, so it compiles only because the including shell already declared the JSTL core prefix c.

Every control in adminPage.jsp is a query-string edit of the current URL: first page ?page.start=0${page.param}, previous ?page.start=${page.start-page.count}${page.param}, page n ?page.start=${status.index*page.count}${page.param}, next ?page.start=${page.start+page.count}${page.param} and last ?page.start=${page.last}${page.param}; unavailable controls get class="disabled" on the li and are made unclickable by a jQuery handler on ul.pagination li.disabled a.

adminPage.jsp reads exactly the Page EL names page.param, page.totalPage, page.total, page.start, page.count, page.last, page.hasNext and the misspelled page.hasPreviouse, the last matching the equally misspelled Java getter isHasPreviouse(); because EL renders an unresolvable name as false or empty rather than failing, renaming only one side would silently leave the previous-page controls permanently disabled.

The numbered page links are filtered to a sliding row-offset window: a page number renders only when status.count*page.count-page.start lies between -10 and 20, which with count=5 shows at most seven page numbers around the current slice.

Page.param is set by exactly two actions — ProductAction#list and PropertyAction#list — both to the exact string "&category.id=" + category.getId(); the other three paged lists (category, user, order) leave it null, which the JSP EL renders as an empty string.

page.param must begin with '&' because adminPage.jsp concatenates it directly onto a complete href="?page.start=…", and it must be repeated on every generated link because each link replaces the whole query string; without it the parent-scoped list actions receive no parent key, so ProductAction#list and PropertyAction#list dereference a null category (and query by a null parent) and fail instead of listing an unscoped page.

All five paged list actions repeat the same four steps — substitute new Page() when no page.start was bound, set page.total from a count method, load rows from listByPage(page) for category/user/order or list(page, parent) for property/product, and return the listXxx forward; OrderAction#list additionally fills each order with its order items.

BaseService declares listByPage(Page) with total(), plus list(Page, Object) with total(Object), as the paging contract, and BaseServiceImpl implements the unfiltered pair on a clazz it derives reflectively from the subclass name (strip the ServiceImpl suffix, swap .service.impl for .pojo): rows come from DetachedCriteria.forClass(clazz) ordered by Order.desc("id") and narrowed by findByCriteria(dc, page.getStart(), page.getCount()), while the total comes from a separate select count(*) HQL over clazz.getName().

The parent-scoped paging variants filter on the parent object's class simple name uncapitalised (Category becomes "category") in both the Restrictions.eq criterion and the count HQL; ProductServiceImpl inherits this implementation unchanged, while PropertyServiceImpl overrides both methods with a literal "category" and bean.category = ?0.

The row slice is applied by HibernateTemplate rather than in Java: ServiceDelegateDAO.findByCriteria(dc, firstResult, maxResults) delegates to the dao bean, which is DAOImpl extending HibernateTemplate; the only in-memory chunking in the tree is ProductServiceImpl.fillByRow's subList rows of 8, which is home-page layout, not paging.

The count query and the slice query are two independent statements issued in that order with no shared snapshot — the list methods carry no @Transactional, only save( ) and createOrder( ) are annotated — so concurrent writes can leave page.total, and the page numbers derived from it, out of step with the rows actually returned.

ProductAction#list computes page.total from propertyService.total(category) — a count of the category's properties — while the rows come from productService.list(page, category), the category's products, so its totalPage, last and numbered links are derived from a count that does not describe the listed rows and can offer pages the product table cannot fill 【人工评审待确认】.

Page.param is an ordinary settable bean property, so Struts binds it from the query string exactly like page.start, and adminPage.jsp writes ${page.param} into the document without escaping, so a hand-built request such as admin_category_list?page.param=x alters the rendered admin HTML.

Storefront search is the foresearch endpoint: web/include/search.jsp and web/include/simpleSearch.jsp both POST a single field named keyword to foresearch and re-populate the box from ${param.keyword}, ForeAction#search passes the keyword to productService.search(keyword, 0, 20), the forward result searchResult.jsp is declared on Action4Result, and "search" is on AuthInterceptor's noNeedAuthPage list so the endpoint is reachable anonymously.

ProductServiceImpl.search is the only search implementation: a DetachedCriteria for clazz with Restrictions.like("name", "%" + keyword + "%") and no Order clause, executed through findByCriteria(dc, start, count), which ForeAction calls with the literals 0 and 20 — a fixed, unstably ordered 20-row window that matches the product name only, so matches beyond the first 20 are unreachable because no storefront page renders a pager.

The search keyword is interpolated into the LIKE pattern rather than escaped, so % and _ inside it behave as wildcards (a keyword of "%" matches every product), and because ForeAction#search does not null-check keyword, a bare GET /foresearch runs name LIKE '%null%' because string concatenation turns the null into the text "null".

productsBySearch.jsp tests ${empty ps} for its empty state even though the action populates products and no ps attribute exists anywhere in the tree, so the 没有满足条件的产品 block is emitted on every search response, including a successful one.

No filtering other than the product-name substring is evidenced for search: the predicate touches only name, the category strip rendered by the search box links to forecategory rather than to a narrowed search, and foresearch reads neither sort nor a category key; whether the missing filters, the 20-row cap and the absent ordering are intended is unsettled 【人工评审待确认】.
